claim: The FBI's San Antonio Division handles FBI matters in Corpus Christi (spokesperson Mark Ellery).
note: Corpus Christi resident agency (Nueces, San Patricio, Aransas, Kleberg and 13 other counties) belongs to FBI Houston. Fixed in RW-001..RW-013; canon.json and characters.json also say San Antonio and need the same change.

claim: Federal prosecutions in Corpus Christi are handled by the US Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Texas.
note: SDTX Corpus Christi Division covers Nueces, San Patricio, Aransas, Kleberg and others.

claim: FEMA Region 6 serves Texas.
note: Region 6 (Denton, TX): AR, LA, NM, OK, TX.

claim: Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi is the local Coast Guard command; its commander as Captain of the Port decides channel closures and reopening.
note: 33 CFR 165.804 gives the Corpus Christi COTP port-condition and vessel-movement authority.

claim: Coast Guard and Texas General Land Office form a Unified Command for a coastal oil spill; the GLO runs the state oil spill program.
note: GLO is the state lead under the Oil Spill Prevention and Response Act of 1991; USCG is federal on-scene coordinator.

claim: CISA has regional cybersecurity advisors and supports the Coast Guard on maritime cyber incidents; Coast Guard and CISA issue joint advisories.
note: CISA regional cybersecurity advisors are a real role; joint USCG/CISA maritime advisories exist. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: The FAA issues notices to pilots about GPS interference and sets drone airspace rules; federal rules restrict drone flights over many military installations.
note: FAA NOTAMs cover GPS interference testing/events; 14 CFR 99.7 special security instructions restrict UAS over listed DoD facilities. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: The Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District is the local health department.
note: Real agency name. Whether it currently runs wastewater surveillance was not confirmed (scenario detail).

claim: The Nueces County Office of Emergency Management issues preparedness guidance and evacuation information.
note: Real county office (Emergency Management & Risk Management); the City of Corpus Christi also has its own OEM.

claim: The National Weather Service has a forecast office in Corpus Christi.
note: NWS WFO Corpus Christi (CRP). (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: A federal inspector general audits and investigates fraud, waste and abuse and reports to agency leadership and Congress.
note: Accurate general description. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: The state closes fishing and shellfish harvesting in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays after the spill.
note: Shellfish harvest-area closures in Texas are issued by DSHS; finfish closures for oil are unusual. Stories say 'the state', which is safe; avoid attributing the closure decision to the GLO.

claim: Oil spill damage claims are filed through a process opened by state spill officials (GLO).
note: Under OPA 90 and 31 TAC 19.53, claims go first to the responsible party; the GLO's Coastal Protection Fund is a backstop. Stories never mention the responsible party. Not fixed (scenario PUB-082), but worth one sentence if P063-02 is revised.

claim: Corpus Christi Army Depot sits on NAS Corpus Christi and is DoD's primary rotary-wing (helicopter) repair depot, one of the region's largest employers.
note: Largest rotary-wing repair facility in the world; largest tenant on NAS CC.

claim: NAS Corpus Christi hosts Navy flight training squadrons flying turboprops and a Coast Guard air station as a tenant.
note: TRAWING 4: T-6B (VT-27/28) and T-44C (VT-31/35); CG Air Station Corpus Christi is a tenant.

claim: Jets climb out over Flour Bluff from NAS Corpus Christi.
note: NAS CC trainers are turboprops; jets are at NAS Kingsville. Fixed RW-020/021.

claim: NAS Corpus Christi sits at the end of Ocean Drive, between Corpus Christi Bay and Oso Bay, beside Flour Bluff and the Laguna Madre.
note: Ocean Drive ends at the north gate; base bounded by Corpus Christi Bay, Oso Bay and Laguna Madre side of Flour Bluff.

claim: NAS Kingsville, southwest of Corpus Christi, trains Navy jet pilots.
note: Training Air Wing 2, T-45C Goshawk.

claim: NAS Corpus Christi and NAS Kingsville fly training aircraft to NAS Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth ahead of hurricanes; Navy air stations did this before Harvey in 2017.
note: NAS JRB Fort Worth is the designated safe haven; NAS CC flew T-6s and T-44s there for Harvey.

claim: NAS Corpus Christi, NAS Kingsville and NAS JRB Fort Worth fall under Navy Region Southeast.
note: CNRSE oversees the three Texas installations.

claim: DLA Distribution Corpus Christi supplies parts to Corpus Christi Army Depot.
note: Primary wholesale distribution point for CCAD helicopter components.

claim: The Army post near Killeen is named Fort Hood.
note: Redesignated from Fort Cavazos back to Fort Hood in June 2025 (now honoring Col. Robert B. Hood).

claim: The Port of Corpus Christi is a DoD-designated strategic seaport that has handled Army deployments for decades; Fort Hood units ship equipment through it.
note: Designated December 1997; e.g., 2017 Apache outload by the 842nd Transportation Battalion.

claim: Fort Hood is a few hours' drive from Corpus Christi.
note: About 290-300 road miles, roughly 4.5-5 hours.

claim: Fort Hood is 250 miles north of the port.
note: About 230 miles straight-line, about 290-300 by road. Fixed RW-024.

claim: Unit equipment moves by rail and road to the port, is staged, and loads on roll-on/roll-off sealift ships; helicopters are wrapped against salt air.
note: Matches SDDC/842nd Transportation Battalion practice at Port CC.

claim: Navy families report status in the Navy Family Accountability and Assessment System (NFAAS); Military OneSource offers free confidential counseling.
note: Both are real programs. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: The C-17 is the Air Force's main strategic cargo jet able to land outsized loads on shorter runways.
note: Accurate. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: The Port of Corpus Christi is the largest US crude export gateway, handling about half of US crude exports.
note: Port reports about 60%; 'about half' is a reasonable scenario value.

claim: Crude reaches Corpus Christi terminals by pipeline from the Permian Basin / West Texas; terminals sit at Ingleside and along the Inner Harbor.
note: Accurate.

claim: Coast Guard port conditions are set by when gale-force winds are expected; vessels at anchor put to sea and oceangoing ships may have to leave or request permission to stay.
note: WHISKEY 72h, X-RAY 48h, YANKEE 24h, ZULU 12h before gale-force winds; ships 500 GT+ plan to depart by YANKEE unless the COTP authorizes.

claim: Fourteen vessels were still holding at the offshore anchorage east of Port Aransas when the Category 3 storm hit.
note: Ships at an open anchorage at the landfall point would put to sea; the stories' own explainers say so. Fixed RW-016..RW-019.

claim: Keeping laden tankers alongside through a storm is decided case by case with the Captain of the Port.
note: COTP may authorize vessels to remain in port.

claim: Recreational boaters must not impede vessels that can navigate only within the channel; small craft are not required to broadcast AIS.
note: Inland Rule 9(b); AIS carriage applies to commercial vessels of set sizes, not most small craft. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: Reopening a channel after a hurricane needs hydrographic surveys, aids-to-navigation checks and dock assessments before the COTP lifts restrictions.
note: Standard post-storm port recovery sequence.

claim: The Harbor Bridge carries US 181 over the ship channel between downtown and North Beach; the Nueces Bay Causeway carries it to Portland.
note: North Beach has two road exits: south via the Harbor Bridge, north via the causeway.

claim: North Beach is a narrow strip between Corpus Christi Bay and Nueces Bay with the aquarium and the museum ship (USS Lexington).
note: Texas State Aquarium and USS Lexington are on North Beach.

claim: The JFK Causeway leads to Padre Island, and Highway 361 runs north up Mustang Island to Port Aransas.
note: JFK Causeway carries PR 22 from Flour Bluff; SH 361 starts at PR 22 on Padre Island and runs north to Port Aransas.

claim: State-run (TxDOT) ferries cross the ship channel between Harbor Island and Port Aransas just inside the pass; the landing is described as in Aransas Pass.
note: TxDOT Port Aransas ferry, SH 361. Harbor Island lies partly within Aransas Pass and Port Aransas city limits, so 'landing in Aransas Pass' is acceptable.

claim: The Port Aransas jetties mark the Gulf entrance to the Corpus Christi Ship Channel at the north end of Mustang Island.
note: Aransas Pass entrance channel and jetties at Port Aransas. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: The Inner Harbor runs for miles west of the Harbor Bridge, lined with docks, refineries and tank farms.
note: Accurate. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: The O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant in Calallen, on the Nueces River at the city's northwest edge, is the city's only water treatment plant and also serves neighboring communities.
note: Sole treatment plant (a brackish desal unit at the same site was approved in 2026 but is not assumed online in 2027). Raw water from the Nueces River and Lake Texana via reservoirs.

claim: The Nueces River gauge at Calallen, upstream of Nueces Bay near the treatment plant, is a key river reading.
note: USGS 08211500 Nueces Rv at Calallen.

claim: The Nueces Delta marshes lie 'just upriver from the causeway'.
note: The causeway crosses the east mouth of Nueces Bay; the delta is at the west end. Fixed RW-023.

claim: The Nueces Delta is where the Nueces River spreads into Nueces Bay; it is a nursery for shrimp, crabs and fish.
note: Coastal Bend Bays & Estuaries Program Nueces Delta Preserve.

claim: Corpus Christi and Flour Bluff are in Nueces County; Kingsville is in Kleberg County; Portland and Ingleside are in San Patricio County.
note: Portland is mostly in San Patricio (small part in Nueces); Kingsville is the Kleberg County seat.

claim: Rockport is up the coast in Aransas County; Aransas Pass is a shrimping town by Redfish Bay.
note: Aransas Pass spans San Patricio, Aransas and Nueces counties; Redfish Bay borders it. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: Flour Bluff sits beside the Laguna Madre and Naval Air Station Corpus Christi.
note: Flour Bluff is on the Encinal Peninsula next to NAS CC and the Laguna Madre.

claim: Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi is the local university with coastal oceanographers.
note: Real university (Harte Research Institute, coastal science). (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: Winter Texans arrive on the island in late November.
note: Real seasonal visitors. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: Hurricane Harvey (2017) came ashore near Rockport and was the region's most recent major hurricane; it tore through Port Aransas.
note: Cat 4 landfall on San Jose Island ~5 mi east of Rockport, Aug. 25, 2017; nearly every structure in Port Aransas damaged. No later major hurricane hit the Coastal Bend through 2025.

claim: STEAR (State of Texas Emergency Assistance Registry) lets residents who need evacuation help, including those without a vehicle, register by calling 2-1-1 or online.
note: Registration does not guarantee service; must be renewed annually.

claim: New flood insurance policies usually take 30 days to take effect; homeowners policies usually exclude flood.
note: NFIP 30-day waiting period with limited exceptions.

claim: Texas boil-water notices: bring water to a rolling boil for two minutes.
note: TCEQ standard language.

claim: Boil tap water at a rolling boil for one minute (Corpus Christi notice).
note: Contradicts TCEQ language, PUB-039 and every other story. Fixed RW-014/015.

claim: Under a boil-water notice: discard tap-water ice, boil water for formula, coffee and brushing teeth; showering is OK if water is kept out of the mouth.
note: Matches TCEQ GI-431 and CDC guidance.

claim: Hand sanitizer is not enough against norovirus; stay home two days after symptoms end; clean with bleach.
note: CDC guidance (48 hours).

claim: Wastewater testing tracks community trends of viruses such as norovirus, not individual cases.
note: Accurate description of wastewater surveillance.

claim: FEMA individual assistance: register online, by phone or at a disaster recovery center; FEMA never charges a fee; have ID, SSN, insurance, bank details, proof of occupancy for renters.
note: Matches FEMA registration guidance. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: FEMA individual assistance registration opened two months (60 days) after a Category 3 landfall.
note: Scenario value (PUB-081) but procedurally implausible: IA registration opens when the declaration includes IA, usually within days (Beryl 2024 IA added 2-3 days after declaration). Flagged needs_rewrite RW-025.

claim: Texas law lets counties skip competitive bidding for purchases necessary to preserve or protect public health or safety; federal rules allow noncompetitive emergency contracts only for the duration of the emergency.
note: Tex. Local Gov't Code 262.024(a)(2); 2 CFR 200.320(c)(3) exigency.

claim: County records can be requested under the Texas Public Information Act; federal contract awards are in public databases.
note: Accurate. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: Debris contracts are paid by volume or weight, tracked by load tickets and monitors; sort curbside debris into vegetation, construction, appliances, electronics and household hazardous waste.
note: Matches FEMA debris management guidance. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: A federal search warrant is signed by a judge on probable cause and charges no one; civil forfeiture targets property, not people.
note: Accurate. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: Credential stuffing uses username/password pairs leaked elsewhere, tried automatically against a new site; defenses are unique passwords and multifactor sign-in.
note: Accurate. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: Atlantic hurricane season runs June 1 to Nov. 30 and peaks in early to mid-September; busiest stretch mid-August into October.
note: NHC glossary; climatological peak about Sept. 10.

claim: A hurricane watch is usually issued about 48 hours before tropical-storm-force winds; a warning about 36 hours ahead.
note: NHC glossary wording.

claim: The scenario's hurricane watch was issued Thursday for a Tuesday 1 a.m. landfall (about four days ahead).
note: Inconsistent with the 48-hour rule; scenario-level, flagged low needs_rewrite RW-026.

claim: Rapid strengthening means sustained winds increase at least 35 mph (30 kt) within 24 hours.
note: NHC: at least 30 kt in 24 h.

claim: The cone shows the probable track of the center, built from past forecast errors; the center stays inside about two-thirds of the time; impacts extend outside it.
note: Circles sized to contain 2/3 of historical errors.

claim: Storm surge is measured in feet above normally dry ground, is the deadliest hurricane hazard, and NWS/NHC issues separate storm surge watches and warnings.
note: NHC storm surge watch/warning products; surge historically causes about half of US hurricane deaths.

claim: In a surge, water piles into shallow Corpus Christi and Nueces bays; surge stacks on top of the tide; compound flooding when rain/river meets surge.
note: Accurate general description (storm tide = surge + astronomical tide). (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: Hurricane kits: at least one gallon of water per person per day for several days; never run a generator indoors or in a garage.
note: Ready.gov guidance. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: Rip currents: swim parallel to shore to escape.
note: NWS guidance. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: GPS satellites orbit roughly 12,500 miles up and their signals are faint at Earth, so a stronger signal on the same frequencies can drown them out.
Radar (SAR) satellites see through clouds; smooth floodwater appears dark.
note: Specular reflection from calm water returns little signal. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: Day 0 is Tuesday Sept. 14, 2027; Labor Day 2027 is Monday Sept. 6.
note: Checked with Python calendar. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: 2027 holiday dates as used: Halloween Sunday Oct. 31; Veterans Day Thursday Nov. 11; Thanksgiving Nov. 25; Black Friday Nov. 26; Giving Tuesday Nov. 30; Pearl Harbor Remembrance Day Tuesday Dec. 7; Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe Sunday Dec. 12; Christmas Saturday Dec. 25.
note: Weekdays checked against story days with Python. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: Daylight saving time ends at 2 a.m. Sunday Nov. 7, 2027.
note: First Sunday in November. (Standard reference; verified from general knowledge, page not fetched this session.)

claim: The Perseids, debris from a comet, peak overnight Thursday Aug. 12 into Friday Aug. 13, 2027, with moonlight reducing counts.
note: Peak night Aug. 12-13; waxing gibbous moon about 80%.

claim: The Geminids peak Monday night Dec. 13 into Tuesday Dec. 14, 2027, and watchers under dark skies can see dozens an hour.
note: Date right, but the 2027 peak coincides with full moon (IMO: 'Full Moon for the Geminids'); guide omits it. Fixed RW-022.

claim: Venus, planets and satellites are what skywatchers mistake for unusual lights in December 2027.
note: Venus passed superior conjunction Aug. 2027 and is an evening object by December.
